subject: Hosting inclusion & routing: SOC 2 audit overlap / bridge guidance
messages:
From: Amir Rahman <amir@finservcorp.com>
To: logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finservcorp.com, security@finservcorp.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify audit applicability for hybrid hosting (routing question)

Hi Logan,

Quick question as we prepare our SOC 2 intake: our deployment will route production traffic to your Hosted API for most customers, but a subset of premium customers will be routed to our Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) and a small number will sit in customer-managed VPCs via Redwood Private. The security team is asking two things:

- For the forthcoming SOC 2 Type II, can you confirm which hosting modes are explicitly covered in the report period?
- For clients that are routed dynamically between Hosted and Dedicated (routing based on latency/cost policies), do we need a separate bridge letter or evidence showing that routing decisions do not expose control gaps during the audit window?

We'd like a short written statement we can attach to our control mapping. If easier, a draft bridge note we can share with our auditors would be ideal.

Thanks,
Amir
Security Lead
FinServ Corp

[attachment: planned-deployment-topology.pdf (stub)]

From: logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Rahman <amir@finservcorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit applicability for hybrid hosting (routing question)

Hi Amir — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer up front: for the 2027 Type II period we can confirm Hosted API and Dedicated (reserved) pools are in-scope; customer-managed VPC/on-prem environments are out of scope for Redwood's Type II report unless the customer opts into our Private offering and we manage the control plane as defined in the attestation.

A few clarifications that will help your auditors map controls:

- Hosted API: covered for the audit window. Controls around change management, access, logging, and incident response are exercised against the hosted tenancy.
- Dedicated pools (reserved capacity): included when the pool is operated by Redwood. We include tenant isolation, capacity controls, and operational procedures in the Type II testing for Dedicated.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: out-of-scope unless the deployment is the Redwood Private managed variant (we do limited managed installs). For customer-self-managed VPCs, customers are responsible for environment-level controls and we provide integration evidence (logs, API access controls) as applicable.

On routing: dynamic routing between Hosted and Dedicated does not by itself create a coverage gap provided the requests that land in Dedicated are processed on Redwood-managed capacity (i.e., the Dedicated pool is in-scope). The thing auditors often ask for is an explicit description of routing policy and examples showing how data residency and tenancy boundaries are preserved during failover or burst events.

I'll loop in Karthish (karthik_iyer) who manages our compliance artifacts to draft a short bridge note and a one-page mapping you can attach. Neha from Solutions will add a simple topology example showing a routing decision timeline (prefix cache / KV behavior) so auditors can see the control handoff.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify audit applicability for hybrid hosting (routing question)

Thanks Logan — super helpful. A couple of follow-ups from the security review:

1) For Dedicated: our auditor wants assurance that "burst" routing (short-term overflow from Hosted to Dedicated and vice versa) retains the same control set (log collection, key management, KV cache handling). Can you point to specific evidence we can attach?

2) For customers in a VPC that use Redwood Private managed control plane (not self-managed), can you confirm whether the Private install was included in the 2027 test population or if it requires a separate attestation?

If you can share a draft bridge-letter and the list of evidentiary artifacts (log retention policy, sample runbook excerpts, key rotation dates) that would speed review.

Cheers,
Amir

Subject: Re: Clarify audit applicability for hybrid hosting (routing question)

Hi Amir — Karthik here from Compliance. Attaching a concise bridge-letter draft and an evidence checklist to help your auditor. Key responses below: 

- Burst routing and control parity: when a request is routed between Hosted and a Redwood-managed Dedicated pool, the same logging pipeline, KMS-backed key handling, and runtime isolation controls are applied. We capture request-level telemetry with the same retention and hashing policy across both hosting modes; sample log extracts are on the checklist.

- Private (managed) installs: our managed Private deployments are included in the Type II testing only when explicitly listed in the customer cohort for that engagement. For 2027 we included three managed Private installs (listed in the bridge draft); if your Private install is customer-managed you'll need to scope those controls yourself and we can provide integration evidence but not an attestation.

- Attachments: bridge-letter-draft.docx (editable draft), redwood-soc2-typeii-summary-2027.pdf (summary and tested control list), and an evidence-checklist.csv (sample artifacts + retention windows).

Next steps: please confirm whether FinServ's Private deployment is customer-managed or Redwood-managed and we'll finalize the bridge wording. If helpful we can schedule a 30-min call with the auditor to walk the checklist.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
